quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other — either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other — either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: When you need to brake and swerve, do them separately. Never brake while swerving because this can make your motorcycle tip over.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit with your arms straight when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Keep your elbows slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank to help you stay balanced.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle is going or how far away it is. Do not assume that drivers of large vehicles can judge your speed and location correctly.

questions.question: The center of a lane has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Should be avoided at all times.
Usually gives good traction, unless it is raining.
Should only be used if you share the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually gives good traction, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip is usually oily, but it still gives good traction for riding unless it is raining. The strip is usually less than two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: If you are in a crash that causes more than $1,000 in property damage, you must:

options.text: File a report only if you plan to report it to your insurance company.
Submit a crash report to the DMV.
Contact the highway department.

questions.correctAnswerText: Submit a crash report to the DMV.
questions.explanation: You must report any crash with property damage over $1,000 to the DMV. The DMV can take action if there was no insurance.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a green arrow before turning in that direction.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Stay farther back from other vehicles.
Ride closer to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and stay farther back from the vehicle ahead. Use the headlights of other vehicles to see ahead. Be ready to change your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: Motorcycles towing trailers:

options.text: Cannot use carpool lanes.
Can use any lane on a highway.
Must go no faster than 25 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot use carpool lanes.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles towing trailers are not allowed in carpool lanes. They should stay in the right lane, except when passing. Do not go faster than 55 mph when towing a trailer.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: During the day.
At dusk.
At night.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright colors and reflective materials, even in daylight.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up quickly as it gets close.
Swerve around the dog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up quickly as it gets close.
questions.explanation: If you see a dog approaching, slow down and downshift until you are near the dog. Then speed up quickly to get away from it.

questions.question: Is eye protection required?

options.text: Yes, required for all riders.
No, but it is recommended.
Only for inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all motorcycle riders to wear eye protection. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns you about a divided roadway coming up.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is slippery.
When the sun is shining.
When you can stop easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when the pavement is slippery, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy. Your motorcycle will need more distance to stop safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: How should you instruct your passenger to sit?

options.text: Board the motorcycle before you do.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Start the engine before your passenger boards. They should sit as far forward as comfortable and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should you wear to protect your hearing while riding?

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.
A baseball cap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a full-face helmet. Use hearing protection to stay safe.

questions.question: How should you look through a turn?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders.
Turn just your head.
Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn by turning only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when being passed?

options.text: The right side of your lane
The center of your lane
The left side of your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of your lane
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving closer to the passing vehicle creates a dangerous situation for both of you.

questions.question: How many wheels can a motorcycle have?

options.text: No more than two wheels.
No more than three wheels.
No more than four wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: No more than three wheels.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is defined as a motor vehicle with a seat for the rider and no more than three wheels.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle in a curve?

options.text: The outside of the curve
The inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Each curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the road and traffic conditions, and adjust as needed.

questions.question: What is a main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for the weather.
Turning too wide in a curve.
Leaving the road to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-vehicle crashes is turning too wide in a curve. Turning too wide can push a motorcycle off the road or into an object.

questions.question: What formation should you use when riding in a group?

options.text: Always ride single-file.
It depends on the situation.
Always ride staggered.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: Generally, groups should ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, entering highways, or leaving highways.

questions.question: What should you do when riding over grooved pavement in a work zone?

options.text: Look down to watch for road changes.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding through a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle gives the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both front and rear brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: What license do you need to operate a moped?

options.text: Class M1
Class M2
Class C

questions.correctAnswerText: Class M2
questions.explanation: A Class M2 license lets you operate motorized bicycles, mopeds, and motorized scooters. A Class M1 license lets you operate all of these plus two-wheel motorcycles. A Class C license is for motorcycles with side cars, three-wheel motorcycles, or motorized scooters.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, if you arrive at the same time as another driver, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What is true about operating a motorized scooter?

options.text: You can only operate it during the day.
You do not need a driver license.
You can operate it with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can operate it with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: What causes an engine to seize?

options.text: Low oil.
Low fuel.
Incorrect tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low oil.
questions.explanation: Engines seize when oil is low. Without oil, the engine's moving parts cannot slide smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely and go when safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Other vehicles will enter the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians cross, and then go when it is safe.
